result.summary: Strengthens tapscript asset test vectors by adding 0-of-0 OP_CHECKMULTISIG and OP_CHECKMULTISIGVERIFY test cases in feature_taproot.py, ensuring failure is triggered specifically by opcode disabling rather than DER signature validation failure. Also exports the expected script error into script_assets_test.json and verifies it in script_assets_test under the exact flag set.
result.problem: Existing tapscript test cases for disabled OP_CHECKMULTISIG and OP_CHECKMULTISIGVERIFY used Schnorr signatures that failed DER signature checks even if an implementation mistakenly executed the opcodes. Additionally, failure test cases in script_assets_test.json did not specify the expected script error, meaning tests could pass even if an execution failed for the wrong reason.
evidence: Author note in PR description: 'This came up while running script_assets_test.json against a third-party implementation which executed OP_CHECKMULTISIG in tapscript and passed every case.'
result.scope_notes: Modifies test generation in feature_taproot.py and updates verification in script_assets_test; changes the schema of script_assets_test.json to optionally include an 'error' field.
result.card: Adds 0-of-0 OP_CHECKMULTISIG and OP_CHECKMULTISIGVERIFY cases to feature_taproot.py and records expected error strings in the generated script_assets_test.json asset dump. The existing tests used Schnorr signatures that failed DER validation, allowing buggy third-party implementations that still executed the disabled opcodes to pass all test vectors. The author discovered this when testing an implementation that executed CHECKMULTISIG in tapscript yet passed all prior asset tests. Test verification now checks that failure cases fail with the exact expected script error.

risk.why: Touches only functional test generation and unit test verification scripts without altering consensus, validation, or node runtime logic.
